ORDINANCE NO. 4 OF 2022

AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING THE ISSUANCE OF A PROMISSORY
NOTE TO PROVIDE FINANCING FOR FITNESS EQUIPMENT FOR THE
CABOT VETERANS PARK COMMUNITY CENTER EXPANSION;
AUTHORIZING THE SALE OF THE NOTE AND THE EXECUTION OF A
NOTE PURCHASE AGREEMENT; DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND
PRESCRIBING OTHER MATTERS PERTAINING THERETO

WHEREAS, the City of Cabot, Arkansas (the "City") is authorized and empowered under
the provisions of Amendment No. 78 to the Arkansas Constitution ("Amendment No. 78"), to
issue notes and to expend the proceeds thereof to finance the cost of acquiring and constructing
real property or tangible personal property having an expected useful life of more than one (1)
year; and

WHEREAS, the City proposes to borrow monies to provide fitness equipment for the
Veterans Park Community Center Expansion (the "Veterans Park Community Center Expansion
Project"); and

WHEREAS, it is proposed that the City issue its Promissory Note (Veterans Parks
Community Center Expansion Project) in the principal amount of $217,638.32 (the "Note")
under Amendment No. 78 for the purpose of financing the Veterans Park Community Center
Expansion Project; and

WHEREAS, the City has made arrangements with First Arkansas Bank & Trust (the
"Purchaser") to purchase the Note; and

WHEREAS, a copy of the hereinafter described Note Purchase Agreement has been
presented to and is before this meeting.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the City Council of the City of Cabot,
Arkansas:

SECTION 1: The City Council hereby finds that the Veterans Park Community Center
Expansion Project will have a useful life of more than one (1) year, that the City has incurred
three obligations under Amendment No. 78: (1) a note dated February 1, 2018 in the amount of
$267,264 for the Pool Pak at the Veterans Park Community Center; (2) a note dated September
10, 2019 in the amount of $652,000 for the purchase of Astro Turf (the “Astroturf Project”) for
Cabot Parks and Recreation; and (3) a noted dated November 4, 2019 in the amount of $250,000
for the purchase of roof repairs (the “Municipal Building Repairs”) (collectively, the "Three
Outstanding Notes"); and that the principal amount of the Note and the Three Outstanding Notes
do not exceed five percent (5%) of the assessed value of taxable property located within the City
as determined by the last tax assessment.

SECTION 2: The issuance of the Note in the principal amount of $217,638.32 is hereby
authorized. The Note shall be dated the date of issuance and shall bear interest on the outstanding
principal amount at the rate of 2.389% per annum. Payment of principal and interest shall be
monthly, commencing one month from the date the Note is issued. The Note shall be subject to

j

--- page 8 (OCR) ---
prepayment prior to maturity, in whole or in part, at the option of the City, at any time without
penalty.

SECTION 3: The Note shall be sold to the Purchaser for the purchase price of 100% of
par, upon the terms and conditions set forth in a Note Purchase Agreement by and between the
City and the Purchaser (the "Note Purchase Agreement"). The Mayor and City Clerk-Treasurer
are hereby authorized to execute, acknowledge and deliver the Note Purchase Agreement and the
Note for and on behalf of the City. The Note Purchase Agreement and the Note are hereby
approved in substantially the form submitted to this meeting, and the Mayor is hereby authorized
to confer with the Purchaser in order to complete the Note Purchase Agreement and the Note in
substantially the forms submitted to this meeting with such changes as shall be approved by such
persons executing the documents, their execution to constitute conclusive evidence of such
approval.

SECTION 4: As provided in Amendment No. 78, the annual debt service payments on
the Note in each fiscal year shall be charged against and paid from the general revenues of the
City for such fiscal year. For the purpose of making the annual debt service payments, there is
hereby, and shall be, appropriated to pay the Note, an amount of general revenues of the City
sufficient for such purposes. The City Treasurer is hereby authorized and directed to withdraw
from the General Fund of the City and/or from such other sources as may be hereafter directed
by the City Council, the amounts and at the times necessary to make the monthly debt service
payments on the Note and to make such payments in accordance with the Note Purchase
Agreement.

SECTION 5: (a) The City covenants with the Purchaser that it shall not take any action
or suffer or permit any action to be taken or condition to exist which causes or may cause the
interest payable on the Note to be included in gross income for federal income tax purposes.
Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the City covenants with the Purchaser that the
proceeds of the sale of the Note will not be used directly or indirectly in such manner as to cause
the Note to be treated as an "arbitrage bond" within the meaning of Section 148 of the Internal
Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the "Code").

(b) The City represents to the Purchaser that it will not use or permit the use of the
Veterans Park Community Center Expansion Project or the proceeds of the Note, in such manner
as to cause the Note to be a "private activity bond" within the meaning of Section 141 of the
Code. In this regard, the City covenants with the Purchaser that (i) it will not use (directly or
indirectly) the proceeds of the Note to make or finance loans to any person, and (ii) that while
the Note is outstanding the Veterans Park Community Center Expansion Project will only be

used by state and local governmental entities and by other persons on a basis as members of the
general public.

(c) The Note is hereby designated as a "qualified tax-exempt obligation" within the
meaning of the Code. The City represents to the Purchaser that the aggregate principal amount of
its qualified tax-exempt obligations (excluding "private activity bonds" within the meaning of
Section 141 of the Code which are not "qualified 501(c)(3) bonds" within the meaning of Section

145 of the Code), including those of its subordinate entities, issued in calendar year 2022 will not
exceed $10,000,000.

--- page 9 (OCR) ---
(d) The City shall pay any arbitrage rebate due the United States Treasury under
Section 148 of the Code in connection with the Note from moneys in the General Fund of the
City.

(e) The City covenants with the Purchaser that it will not reimburse itself from Note
proceeds for any costs paid prior to the date the Note is issued except in compliance with United
States Treasury Regulation No. 1.150-2 (the "Regulation"). This Ordinance is an "official intent"
within the meaning of the Regulation.

(f) The City covenants with the Purchaser that it will submit to the Secretary of the
Treasury of the United States, not later than the 15th day of the second calendar month after the
close of the calendar quarter in which the Note is issued, a statement concerning the Note which
contains the information required by Section 149(e) of the Code.

SECTION 6: The Mayor and City Clerk-Treasurer, for and on behalf of the City, are
hereby authorized and directed to do any and all things necessary to effect the execution and
delivery of the Note Purchase Agreement and the performance of all obligations of the City
thereunder, the issuance, execution, sale and delivery of the Note, and the performance of all acts
of whatever nature necessary to effect and carry out the authority conferred by this Ordinance.
The Mayor and City Clerk-Treasurer are hereby further authorized and directed, for and on
behalf of the City, to execute all papers, documents, certificates and other instruments that may
be required for the carrying out of such authority or to evidence the exercise thereof.

SECTION 7: The City Clerk-Treasurer is hereby authorized and directed to file in the
office of the City Clerk-Treasurer, as a part of the minutes of the meeting at which this
Ordinance is adopted, for inspection by any interested person a copy of the Note Purchase
Agreement and such document shall be on file for inspection by any interested person.

SECTION 8: The provisions of this Ordinance are hereby declared to be severable, and
if any section, phrase or provision shall for any reason be declared to be invalid, such declaration
shall not affect the validity of the remainder of the sections, phrases and provisions.

SECTION 9: All ordinances, resolutions and parts thereof in conflict herewith are
hereby repealed to the extent of such conflict.

SECTION 10: It is hereby ascertained and declared that the Veterans Park Community
Center Expansion Project is immediately needed for the preservation of the public peace, health
and safety. The Veterans Park Community Center Expansion Project cannot be accomplished
without the issuance of the Note, which cannot be sold at the interest rate specified herein unless
this Ordinance is immediately effective. Therefore, it is declared that an emergency exists and
this Ordinance being necessary for the preservation of the public peace, health and safety shall be
in force and take effect immediately upon and after its passage.

BYLAWS
CABOT YOUTH COUNCIL

Article I: Name and Address

Section 1. The name of this institution shall be the Cabot Youth Council.

Article II: Purposes

Section 1. The Cabot Youth Council is to collect local youth concerns in
items of civic interest and need and to present those concerns to
the Mayor and City Council, as appropriate.

Section 2. The Cabot Youth Council is to educate and guide efforts that
benefit the youth of Cabot; and to work in coordination with
existing youth programs to implement youth driven solutions to
issues the Cabot Youth Council identifies.

Article III: Membership

Section 1. The Cabot Youth Council shall be composed of representatives
from 9" to 12™ grade, of whom reside in, or around, Cabot,
Arkansas. It shall be led by a Youth Council Coordinator

Council Coordinator and approved by the Mayor. Suggestions
for representatives may be solicited from Cabot City Council
Members or other interested individuals. The Youth Council
Coordinator shall be chosen by the Mayor.

Section 3. The number of representatives serving on the Cabot Youth
Council shall be at the discretion of the Cabot Youth Council
Coordinator at the start of each Cabot Youth Council Term, with
the approval of the Mayor.

a yearly basis. Unless altered by the Cabot Youth Council
Coordinator, applications will open in August and members will
begin their term in September. Terms will last until April of the

Staff Summary of SUP Application Submittal Package: f t
The applicant submittal package provides applicable UDC references as it relates to Wireless
Telecommunication Facilities and Tower Use Permit (TUP) requirements. Given that the application is for
construction of a new monopole tower, it is not eligible for administrative review or approval. Therefore, the
applicant has applied for Special Use Permit (SUP) to allow the construction of a new, 149-foot-tall monopole
telecommunications tower. The proposed 149 feet is below the maximum 150 feet allowed for such facilities in
the C-2 zoning district. There are no ‘guy-wires’ proposed to support the structure. The applicant has also
submitted documentation attesting to the need for the tower at this location.
While the proposed tower site is located outside the coverage areas for nearby towers, through technical review,
it was noted by the City Attorney that there was potential for the applicant to utilize an existing public utility tower
(water tower) to meet their service needs. In response, the applicant provided documentation showing that the
co-location site would not meet their coverage goals.
The proposed site is located to the rear of existing commercial buildings to the east and south and is otherwise
surrounding by mature trees and vegetation to the north and west of the tower site. Existing access drive to the
tower site will be utilized, which derives ingress/egress from S. Pine Street. This access drive is not expanding,
there are no additional curb-cuts / access cuts proposed, and there will not be any artificial lighting except that
may be required by the FAA. If any lighting is required, it will be for security purposes and directed away from
surrounding properties. The tower and facility will be secured with a 6-foot security fence. No water and/or
sewer is needed for this site, only electric connection, and phone – which is currently available at the site. The
perimeter of the tower site and cabinet will be screened with 27 Leyland Cypress evergreen plantings.

Council Meeting Minutes
March 7, 2022
6:30 p.m.

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on social
distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the
monthly Council Meeting to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508 N. Lincoln, as
advertised. This allowed for spacing between chairs, as suggested. The event
was successfully streamed through YouTube. This meeting may be viewed at
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oHpJp2VkLTo.

During the regularly scheduled Work Session prior to this meeting, the Council
voted to hold the Council Meeting first as a courtesy to the Girl Scouts in
attendance for the Mayoral Proclamation.

at 6:32 p.m. Council Member James Reid led the prayer and Council Member
Stephen Redd led the Pledge of Allegiance.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present:
James Reid, Matt Webber, Ed Long, Ron Waymack and Stephen Redd (via
Zoom). Maggie Cope, Michael Jones and Brandon Hillenburg were absent.
Also in attendance were Mayor Kincade, City Attorney Ben Hooper and City
Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Ben Hooper read a resignation letter from Council Member Michael Jones. A
copy of the letter is attached to these minutes. Ed Long made a motion to
accept the resignation of Michael Jones, second by James Reid. Motion
passed with a Roll Call Vote of 5-0. Ed Long made a motion to declare
Ward 1, Position 2 as vacant. Motion passed with a Roll Call Vote of 5-0.

Motion passed by a Roll Call Vote of 5-0.

City of Cabot – Alicia Wilmoth was here from the City of Cabot. Jay asked her about the check for Thrive that was

Thrive check back and asked if we could do another check for Retail Attractions. She mentioned that it was now listed

WHEREAS, Ark. Code Ann § 14-42-107(b)(1) states that no council member, official, or
municipal employee shall have an interest, directly or indirectly, in the profit of any contract for
furnishing supplies, equipment, or services to the municipality unless the governing body of the
City has enacted an ordinance specifically permitting council members, officials, or municipal
employees to conduct business with the City; and

WHEREAS, the City of Cabot is in need of automotive maintenance and repair and
will likely continue to be in need of such services throughout the coming year. The City is

also in need of additional vehicles and will likely continue to be through the coming year;
and

WHEREAS, Mitch Ward is a commissioner on the Cabot Planning Commission. He is
also the owner of Red River Ford, a company which provides the services the City is in need of
herein; and

WHEREAS, the City desires to do business with Red River Ford for the maintenance

and repair of vehicles and the provision of vehicles at the state bid price during the coming
year.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: Mitch Ward, as owner of Red River Ford, is hereby permitted to conduct
business with the City of Cabot, Arkansas by providing vehicle maintenance, repair, and related
services. He is further authorized to sell vehicles to the City at the appropriate state bid price.
These authorizations are effective for one year from the date of this legislation’s passage.

SECTION 2: The City of Cabot utilizes a variety of vehicles as it serves the residents of
Cabot and they directly benefit the public’s health, safety, and welfare. The City currently has or
will soon have vehicles that are in need of maintenance and repair. The City also needs, and

likely will continue to need, additional vehicles in order to carry out official functions. An

AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, on the 4'" day of April, 2022 a Petition was filed with the City of Cabot
requesting that the entirety of the alleyways on Block 44, Block 54, and Block 55, original town
of Cabot, as set out herein, be vacated and closed; and

WHEREAS, after due notices as required by law, the Council has, at the time and
place mentioned in the notice, conducted a public hearing on the matter and heard all
persons desiring to be heard on the question of the vacating and closing of the alleyways
referenced herein; and

WHEREAS, the Council finds and hereby ordains that due to the nature of the blocks and
alleyways in question, the fact that they are directly adjacent to each other, and the fact that they
are encompassed by land owned wholly by the Petitioner that they shall be treated as a single
alleyway for purposes of this ordinance, and that this single ordinance shall serve to vacate and
close all of the alleyways referenced herein; and

WHEREAS, the Council finds that the vacature and closure of the alleyways referenced
herein is being done for a permissible purpose; namely for the construction of a church building.
This is a purpose for which alleyway vacatures and closures are specifically authorized under
state law. The Council further finds that the alleyways are serving no current practical public
purpose, that the Petitioner is the only landowner that abuts the alleyways in question, and the
property in question would be better utilized to the public benefit as a church building; and

WHEREAS, the Council finds: that the Petitioner has complied with all relevant
provisions of state law, that the Petitioner is seeking the vacature and closure of the relevant
alleyways for a permissible purpose under state law, that the vacature and closure of the

alleyway is necessary or desirable, and that it is in the interest of the people of Cabot for the
alleyways to be vacated and closed; and.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

attached Exhibit “A” and incorporated herein by this reference.

Shelia DeArmond.

General Director Travis Young introduced new staff members Kristy McEroy as the Community

March 2022 financials were presented. JOHN RUDD MOTIONED TO ACCEPT THE MARCH 2022

the Pool Pak and $10,000.00 warranty repairs. Total figures look off but will be where they
should by the end of the first quarter and funds will even out. Credit card processing fees have
increased, and staff will look at ways to pass on the fees. Several commission members asked
that we not charge for usage of the credit card and look at different ways to offset the fees.
ALL SAY AYE, FINANCIALS PASS.

IV.

Programs
BMX – Weather only canceled one weekend race and everything else is going well. Children
with special needs joining the group was discussed. Travis Young will get the group in touch

of races.
Jordan Miller, CPR Programmer, gave the update on parks programs. All sports had several
dates of cancelations due to the weather. Registration for youth tennis, adult flag football, coed volleyball, and adult basketball will open on May 2nd.
Flag Football – The Secretary and Vice President were present to give the report. Two hundred
and ninety-one children have registered to participate in the season with fifty-six coaches
volunteering. The expenses for the group were discussed. The previous board has refused to

Tackle Football Update – The parks department has been meeting with the previous boards for

program coaches to ensure that teaching the fundamentals are following the same guidelines.

Common’s Room
April 19, 2022
PRESENT: Jay Lallu, Stephen Redd, Brian Knowles, Matt Webber, Greg Jones, & Bryan Williamson
GUESTS PRESENT: Travis Young with Parks & Rec., Clint McGue, legal counsel, Gina Jones, admin/collections for A&P,
Alicia Wilmoth, City of Cabot Economic Development, Sarah Brown, Cabot Chamber of Commerce, Amanda Kincade
(Downtown Christmas) and Shelby Glover (Cabot Christmas parade), both with Cabot City Beautiful
Jay Lallu called the meeting to order at 8:32 am
Pledge: Jay Lallu
Prayer: Brian Knowles
Gina Jones gave roll call.
Funding Recaps:
Downtown Christmas: Amanda Kincade was here to give a funding recap of Downtown Christmas. She mentioned that
there was a great turnout and submitted a roster with how the money was spent. Cabot City Beautiful was given $32,000
on behalf of Cabot City Beautiful and they spent all the money. First Security did hot dogs for everyone. Porchlight did
hot cocoa, Red River did S’mores and the city did the sound system and decorations. She said that they get the
ornaments and wreaths at wholesale price through Curly Willow. They did sweatshirts for the volunteers. They did a
window wonderland for the businesses to decorate their windows and the winners were given a prize.
Cabot Christmas Parade: Shelby Glover was here on behalf of Cabot City Beautiful and said that they had 5 bands this
year because the 6th band had to cancel. This was the longest length of parade that they had ever had. It was a great
event with a great turnout. She mentioned that they had a refund to give the A&P for $1,786 and then gave us the check
for the refund.
Minutes- The commissioners reviewed the minutes from the March 2022 meeting. Motion to accept was made by Greg
Jones after taking the line with the business name out in the general discussions portion of the minutes and the 2nd was
made by Brian Knowles, all voted, and March 2022 minutes were accepted.
Financial Report - Jay mentioned that the numbers were down just a bit from the previous month. Motion to accept
the financials was made by Greg Jones and a 2nd made by Stephen Redd. All vote and the March 2022 financials were
accepted.
Chamber Report – Sarah Brown was here and mentioned that our “Bowling for Business was a super success” Our
membership cookout went great as well. She also mentioned that we have been invited to be a sitting member on the
Eagle Scout board review. She said that they voted in the first female in the state of Arkansas. Our Youth Leadership
Council went around to local businesses here in town in March and it was great. It shows these kids some opportunities
that are available here at home. In April, we will be taking them to the state capital. We had our Easter Egg Selfie
Scavenger this past weekend and had a great turn out. We had to move our golf tournament due to rain. We moved it to
May 4th. We had 11 new members in March, which is the biggest that we have quite possibly ever had in one month.
Funding Request – Cabot Parks & Recreation – Travis Young was here. The total funding request is for a total of
$58,916.48, which is broken down into 2 separate ones, it we so choose.
The first request is for $33,857.40 for additional staples, power wash the crack, inject waterproofing form along the
length of crack, install basecrete mesh tape and polymer cement to necessary finish grade for plaster overlay and repair
100 LF of small surface cracks with a two-part epoxy.

The 2nd is to demo waterline around rec pool and spa, demo tile on spa spillover, prepare outer surface of spa for
waterproofing, apply waterproofing material on outer wall of spa, repair tile bed as necessary, install a 6”x 6” waterline
tile on pool and spa, install a 6”x 6” frost proof tile on outer wall of spa, install 6”x 6” frost proof tile on spillover wall
from spa to rec pool. Travis mentioned that after all this work, it would be a brand-new pool.
Motion to fund the full $58,916.48 was made by Brian Knowles and a 2nd was made by Matt Webber. All voted and it
was accepted.
Cabot Parks & Rec – Travis Young said that their first 5K looks to be great, with 112 registered already. Looking at a
2nd 5K around Christmas. There are 2200 participating in spring sports, baseball tournaments are going great.
Memberships for the community center are looking great as well. He said that their goal is to have all the bond projects
completed by June 2023.
City of Cabot Economic Development- Alicia Wilmoth was here and spoke about the city’s community branding
meeting that they had. She said that in 3 months or so, we should be seeing our new logo. They will be putting up new
banners around the town with the new logo as well. Alicia mentioned that there is a website called visitcabot.com that
has not been touched in a long time. She said that the city is also revamping that where it will be very tourism
consistent. The city will be holding a job fair on 4-27-22 from 11-2 at the event center. Lonoke County has at least 450
job openings. There will be over 60 businesses that will be there.
General discussions – Stephen mentioned that Jay, Gina, and he had a conference call with Pay Simple to go over the
fees for using PaySimple. He mentioned that we are not getting a lot of credit card payments but are getting a lot of
ACH payments. “We are charging 2.5% per credit card transaction. On the ACH, it is a .65 ACH fee plus $.75 batch
fee no matter if you have one or twenty and there is a fee that is tacked on top of that of 1.5%” “Right now, we are
doing better using the lockbox.” He said that “we are waiting for them to send us a list of our fees and we will see about
adjusting some of the fees.”
Jay mentioned that he had seen a couple of new B&B rental places that have popped up on Expedia for here in Cabot.
He said that they will not reveal their address until you book it. But he said that if they are doing this, that they need to
pay A&P taxes too. He said that he saw it on SOSarkansas.
Clint said that the one that was so far behind, did come by and pay, but Gina was not in the office, so they said that they
would come back. The two 5 months, he said that Gina had contacted.

BLOCK 44, BLOCK 54, AND BLOCK 55 OF THE ORIGINAL TOWN OF CABOT;
AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, on the 4'" day of April, 2022 a Petition was filed with the City of Cabot
requesting that the entirety of the alleyways on Block 44, Block 54, and Block 55, original town
of Cabot, as set out herein, be vacated and closed; and

WHEREAS, after due notices as required by law, the Council has, at the time and
place mentioned in the notice, conducted a public hearing on the matter and heard all
persons desiring to be heard on the question of the vacating and closing of the alleyways
referenced herein; and

WHEREAS, the Council finds and hereby ordains that due to the nature of the blocks and
alleyways in question, the fact that they are directly adjacent to each other, and the fact that they
are encompassed by land owned wholly by the Petitioner that they shall be treated as a single
alleyway for purposes of this ordinance, and that this single ordinance shall serve to vacate and
close all of the alleyways referenced herein; and

WHEREAS, the Council finds that the vacature and closure of the alleyways referenced
herein is being done for a permissible purpose; namely for the construction of a church building.
This is a purpose for which alleyway vacatures and closures are specifically authorized under
state law. The Council further finds that the alleyways are serving no current practical public
purpose, that the Petitioner is the only landowner that abuts the alleyways in question, and the
property in question would be better utilized to the public benefit as a church building; and

WHEREAS, the Council finds: that the Petitioner has complied with all relevant
provisions of state law, that the Petitioner is seeking the vacature and closure of the relevant
alleyways for a permissible purpose under state law, that the vacature and closure of the

alleyway is necessary or desirable, and that it is in the interest of the people of Cabot for the
alleyways to be vacated and closed; and.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: The Cabot City Council does hereby vacate and close the alleyways on
Block 44, Block 54, Block 55, original town of Cabot, described with greater specificity in the

attached Exhibit “A” and incorporated herein by this reference.

Dear Mayor Kincade:
Reference is made to the City's recent request to incorporate Job 060490, Cabot Hwy. 321
Sidewalks (TAP-21) (S), as a change order into the subject project.
The total Federal-aid Transportation Alternatives Program (TAP) funds awarded to Job 060490
is $ I 17,000 for the construction of 9,050 linear feet of sidewalk along the north side of Highway 321
from Nally Road to the east. The Department is willing to transfer the TAP funds, if the City is willing
to provide all additional costs associated with the construction of sidewalk, currently estimated to be
$145,301.

In order to proceed with this change, it is necessary to modify the Agreement of Understanding
for Job 061509. Therefore, to proceed with this modification, you and the City Attorney must sign and
return the enclosed Supplemental Agreement. Once executed, a copy will be returned to you. Please
also submit a check, made payable to the Arkansas Depaftment of Transportation, in the amount
of$145,301. The City's final cost will be determined by actual charges. Once the agreement is
executed and the check has been received, the Department will complete the change order to include
this work into the subject project. Job 060490 will be canceled.
Thank you for your continued interest in Arkansas' transportation system. If you have any
questions regarding the partnering arrangement, please contact Jessie Jones, Division Engineer Program Management, at (501) 569-2262.

WHEREAS, on May 15, 2019, the City of Cabot (hereinafter called the ''City'') entered into
an Agreement of Understanding with the Arkansas Department of Transportation (hereinafter
called the ''Department'') for the Project; and
WHEREAS, the City has requested to incorporate 9,050 linear feet of sidewalk along the
north side of Highway 321 into the Project from Nally Road to the east; and
WHEREAS, the Department is agreeable to incorporate the sidewalk into the Project with the
assurance that the actions involved will be cost-neutral for the Department; and
WHEREAS, the City has agreed to contribute the additional costs associated with the
sidewalk, estimated to be $262,301; and
WHEREAS, the City was awarded $117,000 in Federal-aid Transportation Alternatives
Program funds on November 3, 2021 for the construction of the sidewalk; and
WHEREAS, the City intends to use these funds as part of its commitment; and
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT UNDERSTOOD, the following modification is made to the
original Agreement of Understanding:
1. Roles and Responsibilities of the City are modified as indicated below:
a. Add Item 3: When requested, provide the Department with funds for construction of
9,050 linear feet of sidewalk along the north side of Highway 321 from Nally Road to
the east.
IT IS HEREBY AGREED, all other conditions of the original Agreement of Understanding
will remain in effect.
